chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Umarat, from Nueym Al-Qazy, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) woke up in the morning and saw a white hair in his beard, so he said: 'The praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, Who has brought me to this stage/age; I did not disobey Allah even for the blink of an eye.'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Ibrahim say when he saw a white hair in his beard?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) greets the morning with gratitude upon seeing a white hair, viewing aging not as a decline but as a divine milestone confirming his steadfastness. He attributes this longevity to his unwavering obedience, having not disobeyed Allah even for the blink of an eye. This highlights the Shia emphasis on viewing natural life processes as signs of divine favor and spiritual success.

en.hubeali: H 15035 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, together, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al-Hassan Bin Umarat, from Nueym Al-Qazy, who has said: ‘Abu Ja’farasws has said:

‘One morning, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> saw a white hair in his<sup>as</sup> beard, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘The Praise is due to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Worlds Who<sup>azwj</sup> Made me reach to this age, and I<sup>as</sup> never disobeyed Allah<sup>azwj</sup> even for the blink of an eye’.
en.sarwar: 589. Aban Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from the one who reported it: ‘Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said:

‘When Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Took Ibrahim (as) as a friend, Gave him (as) good news in private. The Angel of Death came up to him (as) in the image of a young white man, wearing two white robes, with water and oil dripping from his head. So Ibrahim (as) entered the house, but welcomed him outside the house. And Ibrahim (as) was an honourable (Ghayour) man, and whenever he (as) went out for a need, he (as) would lock his (as) door, and takes its keys with him (as). Then he (as) would return and open it. So there was the man (Angel of Death) standing there, as handsome as a man can be. So he (as) grabbed his hand and said: ‘O servant of Allah (azwj), who entered you into my (as) house?’ He said: ‘Its Lord (azwj) Made me enter it’. So he (as) said: ‘Its Lord (azwj) is more deserving of it than I (as) am. So who are you?’ He said: ‘I am the Angel of death’. Ibrahim (as) panicked and said: ‘You have come to me (as) to capture my (as) soul?’ He said: ‘No. Allah (azwj) has Taken a servant as a friend, so I have come to give the good news to him (as). He (as) said: ‘So who is he (as)? I (as) would like to serve him (as) until I (as) die’. He said: ‘You (as) are him (as)’. So he (as) came up to Sara and said to her: ‘Allah (azwj) Blessed and High has Taken me (as) as a friend!’
